lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: I'd like to call this meeting to order. Welcome here, everyone. And council, I have— I've got opening for today. And yesterday after we met with AMM, I had not had an opening ready yet, so I asked my deputy, I said, I don't have an opening. He said, I'll just do something about the new year. It'll be okay. Thank you for supporting me and giving me good advice. Thank you. I decided to do the opening on something like a highlight for me, uh, as, as, as mayor of 2024. And the year of 2024 marked a historic benchmark for Steinbach. As a city, we witnessed a record number of housing permits issued. This reflects our rapid growth and increasing appeal to— as a place to live, work, and raise a family. This milestone demonstrates Steinbach's commitment to accommodating its growing population and underscores its status as a regional hub in southeastern Manitoba. But what lies— but what lies ahead for Steinbach as it builds on its own success? The surge in housing permits signals strong population growth in Steinbach. Steinbach is known for its family-friendly atmosphere, strong community values, and the city has become a more attractive destination for families, retirees and newcomers to Canada with affordable housing options and a high quality of life. I would like to expect the population of Steinbach to continue to climb in the, in the coming years. This growth will likely spur on further demand for houses, services, infrastructure, presenting both opportunities and challenges for the city's administration and council. Economic growth often goes hand in hand with population increases, and Steinbach is no exception. The construction boom tied to the record number of housing permits has already stimulated our local economy, creating jobs in construction, real estate, and related industries. The housing sector thrives, and other sectors such as retail, healthcare, and education are poised to expand to meet the needs of a growing population. Steinbach's entrepreneurial spirit and diverse business community position, position it well to capitalize on it, on this momentum, potentially attracting new industries and investments. Rapid growth inevitably places pressure on existing infrastructure. Roads, schools, recreation facilities, and utilities must keep up, keep up to pace with the needs of a larger population. In response, council has prioritized infrastructure investments to support sustainable growth. Projects such as road expansions and enhanced utility systems are on the horizon. Looking ahead, Steinbach has an opportunity to shape its future as a thriving, inclusive, and sustainable city. Strategic urban planning will be essential to ensure that growth is managed responsibly. Thank you. responsibly. Initiatives such as mixed-use developments, green spaces, and smart growth strategies can help the city maintain its livability while accommodating new residents. Furthermore, fostering community engagement will be key to preserving Steinbach's strong sense of identity and belonging. After a record-setting year for housing permits in 2024, Steinbach is on the brink of of an exciting period of growth and development. By embracing growth and proactively addressing challenges it brings, the city can position itself as a model for balanced and sustainable development. Steinbach's future growth holds promise as it continues to build on its rich heritage and adapt to the demands of a vibrant and expanding community. Thank you. Okay, council, we have the agenda in front of us, looking for a motion to adopt. Councillor Penner?

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor, and for members of council. Administration has been working for several months On an operating agreement with the designated operator for the soon-to-open Southeast Event Centre, and that is Southeast Events Group Inc. As I mentioned, the discussions have been taking place since early 2024, and I am very pleased to present the agreement for council's consideration. Thank you. attached in the package. The agreement is quite lengthy. I don't anticipate going into reading certain sections. However, I have provided a summary for council's information, just noting some of the key components that are included in the agreement. And for example, Section 1.3 deals with the The term of the agreement, which will run for 3 years ending February 14th, 2028. Article 2 mentions items surrounding general operations and the associated activities within the facility and that those activities will be the responsibility of SEG. Section 5.3 mentions SEG's proposed annual operating budgets for the facility. Thank you. And that they will be subject to a council review and approval process. Article 8, for example, will deal with mechanisms for the management and/or disposition of operating surpluses, deficits, or accumulated surplus funds as may arise with the operation of the facility. Article 7 covers some duties that the City of Steinbach has agreed to provide. Thank you. On behalf of the operation of the facility to be billed back to SEG on a cost recovery basis, and that essentially will cover the back of house or ice making and ice-related maintenance activities. There are some significant funding components that are represented in the agreement, which generally are represented in Article 9 that pertains to an annual operating grant funding support. Thank you. City Council originally identified in the memorandum of understanding dated back in 2019 that the city is prepared to commit at least for a 5-year period annual funding up to a maximum of 0.5 mills of the city's general municipal levy, which is the equivalent of approximately $700,000 annually. Other than that, there are some specific references to General operating principles that both the city and SEG have agreed will be adopted or followed in order to support minor and community-based programming within the facility in a manner similar to how the city of Steinbach has traditionally operated the Centennial and T.G. Smith Arenas. With respect to this agreement, Thank you. From administration standpoint, we believe this is an agreement that will put the community and the facility and both SEG and the City of Steinbach in a solid footing and provide an essential framework to follow that hopefully will lead to, to the success of the operation and and a great facility for the community. Recommendation from administration is for council to approve the attached agreement.

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is something that is— the city is doing for the first time that normally The city has operated our recreation facilities through our internal departments, but in this case, we have made an agreement with the Southeast Events Group, SEG, to operate the Southeast Event Centre. This board is made up of people who have a lot of experience in business, and I think that this will, this will work out, will work out quite well. And as the city manager noted, this is a 3-year Agreement and obviously to be renewed afterwards. The operations and the general running of the facility will be the responsibility of SAG, but council still retains oversight over the annual budget. And so council will review and approve proposed operating budgets. The city is agreeing to provide 0.5 mils of the municipal levy. That works out to about $700,000 annually. This is something that we agreed to back in 2019 with the The original memorandum of understanding. So this is consistent with that. Obviously, we recognize with a recreation facility that there is a need for a subsidy. Recreation facilities cost money to run, and so this is— it's not unusual that the city would be making a contribution like this. And SEG has also agreed to follow the operating principles and policies that the city has in place in regards to community-based programming and programming for minors and such, because we want this facility to be as accessible as possible. And so So I appreciate the work of our city staff on this, and I also appreciate the flexibility of the SEG Group. And again, this is the largest project we've ever done in our history as a city, and I think it's appropriate that we have tapped the expertise of these individuals to help us with running the facility. So I'm happy to approve— to move to approve the operating agreement.

lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Uh, thank you, Mr. Mayor. Uh, the, uh, City of Steinbach, along with 20 other municipalities in Manitoba, receive services from the RCMP for municipal policing purposes. And nationally, the RCMP is going through contract negotiations to renew their operating contract or employment contracts. Was to consider sending, or at least adopting and sending a letter to the federal government officials that are responsible for those contract negotiations in order to further the city's and the balance of the Manitoba municipalities receiving RCMP services in order to look after the municipality's best interests. If council is prepared to send that letter, a draft of which is included in the agenda package. Administration would revise it accordingly for the City of Steinbach and send that document off to the federal government as was proposed by the AMM.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Warkentin. Councillor, would you like to proceed? Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I think it makes sense for us to advocate here on behalf of the city So I'll make a motion that the city forward a letter using this as our template to send it to the appropriate officials. I'll make the motion. If there's a seconder, then I'll explain.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. Do we have a seconder? Councillor Penner. Go ahead, Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. We are one of 21 municipalities in Manitoba that have a contract with the RCMP, and the way that it works is that the municipality is responsible for We pay either 70% or 90% of the total cost. Now, because of our size as a city, we have to pay 90% of the total cost. And so we have a certain number of officers. In our case, we pay for 18, and we designate the number of officers we want to have. We then pay for the service. The challenge is that now that the RCMP are entitled to collective bargaining, the federal government negotiates with them. And in the last round of collective bargaining, the federal government negotiated a 23.7% 7% retroactive pay increase, which obviously has a significant impact on municipal budgets. Now, in our city, of course, our staff ensured that we did set some money aside to help cover that cost, but it still leads to, to a liability there that can impact municipalities because we have no control over what amount gets negotiated. And as AMM has noted, the The questionnaire that went out dealing with identifying bargaining priorities for the upcoming round of negotiation, the municipal members on that committee were not consulted about what's going to be in that questionnaire. And certainly because we're paying the bill, we are paying, in our case, 90% of the cost of the contract, and smaller municipalities are paying 70%, we should be getting a lot more say than what we're getting now. Thank you. And so in concert with other municipalities through AMM, it makes sense for us to advocate here and to make it clear that if we're going to continue to paying the bill and we're going to continue to have RCMP as, you know, that we're hiring on a contract basis, we should have some say over what the priorities are in regards to upcoming rounds of collective bargaining because we're the ones who have to pay the bulk of the cost. And so I I think it makes sense for us to use this letter as a template that was helpfully drafted by AMM, revise it to make it specific to our needs as a city, and then send it off to the appropriate federal and provincial officials so that way it's clear that we agree with the other municipalities that have raised concerns on this.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk

So I think it's really important we advocate along with the rest of, uh, AMM, advocate for, um, what's best for our communities.
